answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent network can tie identities to physical optical delay lines encased in subterranean basalt bedrock. Nodes prove existence by resolving time-of-flight challenges from a shared cryptographic beacon through a micro-fabricated lotus resonator. An attacker incurs unavoidable capital and fabrication costs for discrete photonic hardware per identity. However, thermal fluctuations in the substrate degrade delay precision, causing false rejections.
